title: The thick present

data.source: The precision-weighted update of the free energy principle (Friston 2008) and the Kalman filter (1960). Computed, and simulated in the local level model: 3,000 seeded runs of 400 steps, twice.

prediction: The seed rule is the free energy update with its gain frozen: equal to it in a steady world and weaker when trust should change. The free energy account also has two things R5 lacks: a window around the present, which needs a smooth signal, and hindsight, in which the estimate of a moment keeps improving for a few steps after it has passed.
baseline: The precision-weighted update of the free energy principle (Friston 2008), which here is the Kalman filter (1960; Muth 1960), with the running mean as a decoy.
why: All five predictions held. Shared: the seed rule is the fixed-gain case of the free energy update (R5 is an ASSUMPTION in Phoenix). Left over on the free energy side: a changing gain, a window around the present, hindsight. Left over on the CRR side: the cut, which the filter does not have.

forks.salience-weighted seed (wider notes): not in R1 to R6; not tested

weighs: P1 and P2 are identities and would hold in any world.
result: Gradient descent on the free energy landed on the precision-weighted mean. In a steady world the Kalman gain settled at 0.2702; the seed rule with q = 0.7298 had 1.0 times its error, and the best q found was 0.73. The plain running mean had 30.36 times the error. Carrying one number across each revision lost 0.0 nats per step when the world was steady and 0.3374 when the clearness of the observations kept changing. A belief holding only the value of a smooth signal sees 0.8326 ahead; with six generalised coordinates it sees 2.3812. For a rough signal the extra coordinate added nothing. Hindsight cut the error from 0.2702 to 0.1562, nine tenths of it within 4 steps; the seed rule has no hindsight.

framework.name: The free energy principle and active inference

precise_core: Exact in the linear Gaussian case. The general derivation from a Markov blanket has been disputed in print.
proved_by_others: Several independent groups have re-derived, corrected and criticised it (Biehl, Aguilera, Millidge, Buckley and others).
differing_prediction: The principle itself makes none. Process theories built on it, such as predictive coding, do. Phoenix gives it the same logical status as CRR's grammar.
tested: The process theories are tested widely in neuroscience; one study tested the principle on neurons in a dish.
passed: Mixed. Misses are usually absorbed as a wrong generative model.
replicated: Parts of predictive coding replicate. Nothing specific to the principle has been independently replicated, as far as this check knows.
engineering: Dynamic causal modelling is everyday brain-imaging analysis; active inference agents and robots exist as demonstrations.
admits_open_problems: Its authors publish replies and repairs; whether the principle can fail at all is still argued.

precise_core: R1 to R6 are written exactly, with status keys. The parts are free choices: no universal q, ruler, dynamics or memory kernel (Phoenix: OPEN).
proved_by_others: Nobody outside the owner's programme. Phoenix says its own audit is not independent. Tonight's re-checks were made by model workers, not by independent people.
differing_prediction: Only through added bridges (the change clock, the regeneration law). Phoenix: the core has not yet issued a prediction.
tested: The bridges were frozen and scored on held-out real data inside the programme. No outside group has tested anything.
passed: Phoenix: no held-out CRR-specific pass; its result ledger is empty. Tonight's library ledger has no fits.
replicated: None. The one inherited first-level pass did not replicate (Phoenix).
literature: No peer-reviewed paper on CRR is cited anywhere in Phoenix, and none is known to this check.
engineering: Engineering candidates and good-practice rules only. Phoenix grades the method they rest on as known prior art.
admits_open_problems: An OPEN list in the core itself, failures kept on the ledger, and written exit conditions.

status.note: Scores are 0 to 3 on the stated scale. A line marked from_memory was not checked against a source tonight. The total is a count of ticks, not a ranking of truth.
